sections.text: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च
Drona and Bheeshma, Jayadratha and Karna, and other brave warriors - I have condemned them all. Destroy them; fight and fear not. Thy foes shall be crushed.

Sanjaya continued: Having heard these words from the Lord Shri Krishna, the Prince Arjuna, with folded hands trembling, prostrated himself and with choking voice, bowing down again and again, and overwhelmed with awe, once more addressed the Lord.
Arjuna said: My Lord! It is natural that the world revels and rejoices when it sings the praises of Thy glory; the demons fly in fear and the saints offer Thee their salutations.

What is my purpose and destiny? We had been discussing chapter 11. We have seen Arjunas description of what he is seeing, and we have discussed so many times in the last few weeks. What he has seen is everything that he can perceive in this world, all coming together as one, this plurality which is separated from each other.
Now he sees that as one singularity. He also sees all the divine beings which he has just heard of in his Vedic training or from the cultural training. He sees all of them -- Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh -- all of them merged into this one entity.
But he also sees that all these beings are rushing towards the mouth of that supreme being and getting dissolved, disappearing into it. And he comes to this realization that just as the river water is rushing towards the ocean -- intuitively, with inherent nature, not that somebody is propelling it or forcing it, but by its inherent nature. The river water runs from the mountaintops through the plains to the ocean.
Just as the moth instinctively rush towards its death into the flame, river rushes towards the ocean, loses its identity. Mighty river, like Ganges or Yamuna or even Patomak or James, once it disappears into the ocean, there is no identity of the river of its own. It just becomes part of the ocean.
It seems that is the true nature of the river and the moth. So he sees that all the beings are without any hesitation, theyre rushing towards the mouth of this great being and disappearing into it. And then he sees that this great being is seemingly enjoying this act of all these beings disappearing into his mouth, some get stuck.
He makes sure that nobody is left out when we do some task. And we are so happy about it, that we are so proud of that. In the end we try to inspect and say, is there anything left? Thats basically equivalent to licking up whats going into his mouth -- making sure that all these beings are getting dissolved into his own being.
And now Arjuna says, I dont understand any of this. Akyahi me ko bhavan ugrarupaha -- tell me, O being with a very fierce form. Namostu te deva or prasida -- if you want to ask somebody who you are and that person is not smaller than you, you better be a little respectful first.
He does ask and say, I want to know who you are. But first, Namostute devara prasida -- you are the supreme Lord, so I bow down to you, have mercy on me, because I dont understand. I am not capable of understanding who you are.
And vignatum ichami bhavantam adyam -- I have completely and clearly recognized that you are the Adi being. You are the original being. All beings are nothing but the manifestation of you.
They come from you, they go into you. But you are that original Bhavantam adyam. You are that original being.
Vignatum ichami -- I want to know, which in normal terms we say, I want to know God. I know he is the supreme being. At least from my childhood religious training I understood that he controlled this world.
Vigna tam ichami bhavanta madhyam -- even after having this global vision, the cosmic vision, our intellect is not capable of understanding it. Nahi prajanami tavapravratyam -- also, I have no idea why you are doing this activity which I see right now. Isnt that something we ask all the time? I dont know why Bhagawan does this thing, why there is a tsunami, why there is an earthquake, or why Bill Gates and Steve Jobs are successful and not every IT person in this country.
I do not know what you are doing, Bhagwan. I hope you know what you are doing. Basically Arjuna puts it in his word very respectfully saying I want to know you O supreme Being.
I clearly recognize you are the original being, but I also dont understand what you are engaged in right now. I see all these beings going into your mouth and getting crushed. He has also seen -- we have seen -- that all Kauravas are going into his mouth, as well as all the great kings on both sides.
See, anytime we have a vision, we focus on something closer to our own situation. Anytime you have a dream, the dream is always something related to what you were thinking about in the last week or so. So even when he sees this whole cosmic vision, he focuses on the Kauravas going into his mouth.
All the kings from the Kauravas as well as the kings from our side, going into his mouth. He says, I dont understand what you are engaged in right now. And in response to that, Bhagavan says, Kalosmi -- I am time.
Lokaksha Kruta Pravrad daha -- I am engaged in destroying this world. I can see the world from both perspectives. Either I can see it from a constructive perspective or a destructive perspective in nature.
Actually both simultaneously keeps going on. Something gets destroyed, something gets built. I can fix my perspective only on the destruction part and say why this thing is happening.
I can look at the statistics in the newspaper and say how many people die every day and say oh God, billions of people die. I dont know whether millions or billions, but Im sure there are plenty because every several seconds theres somebody dies in the United States. I read somewhere about how many people die every day, and if I look at that and say God, why do you do this? This many people dying every day.
Dont you have better things to do than just killing? Right now Arjuna is just seeing this destruction going on. So Bhagavans answer is also exactly that. Kalaha Asmi, I am all devouring time.
I was born in 1948. In 2012, Im an old man, but sometime in the 2000-somethings I wont be around. Thats what Lokakshaya krita pravadha means.
Youre seeing me destroying this world. As you know, the world as I know right now, is actually rushing towards its own destruction. All my friends and relatives and all of them, one after the other, theyre all rushing towards their own death.
Kalavasmi lokaksha Kruta Prabhradha. From your perspective, Arjuna, I am that all devouring time. Right now what you are seeing is I am engaged in destroying these worlds.
Lokan sama hartum iha pravrutaha ruteapi tvamna Bhavishyanti swarve e avasthitaha pratyanikeshi odaha. Even without you -- now coming down very personally to Arjuna -- Arjuna had said, I dont want to engage in this war. The whole purpose of this divine vision Arjuna wanted to have was connected to all the philosophy Bhagavan gave him in the second chapter about why he should engage in this war.
Bhagavan had said, look, whoever takes birth will die. Beginning they unmanifest, they will manifest for a while, they will unmanifest in the end. So you dont worry about it.
Whatever the little role you are given in this drama, you take part and take credit for it and you dont worry about whos going to die and whos going to survive. But Arjuna was not clear. So he said, well let me see this entire vision now.
He sees the entire vision and then he says I dont understand what are you doing? And Bhagawan basically said, dont worry about it, I am time. Im going to destroy everything in time. Whether you take part in it or not.
Even without you, none of the warriors in front of you shall live. Whether you take part in this war or not is immaterial. Their destiny is to die in time.
Whenever their time will come, they will die. Because I am that all devouring time. Tasmat Utestha Yashola Basva -- all you have to do is take credit for it.
Everybody says Bill Clinton was the best president in his time. We all thrived and our country has this surplus we never had seen in all these times before. And George Bush came and completely messed it all up.
But Ill tell you what, if George Bush was the president at the time when the technology bubble was blowing up, he would have the same credit. He just happened to be at that time a president. And we can blame Obama all we want.
About 8% or 9% unemployment. But even if Bill Clinton is today, he would have the same problem. Because this thing is driven by this cycle, cosmic cycle, economic cycles, whatever the cycle you want to call it, you just happen to be there.
And if youre a smart person, you do your part and take credit. Become that instrument in this giant will of dharma. So therefore Bhagavan said, look, all these people are already killed by me.
Without your help also they will get killed. You just saw that every being is rushing towards their death in my mouth. Get up Yashola Basra and get the fame that you deserve.
Jitva Satrun Bhangshvarajam Samruddham -- get victory over your enemies and enjoy the kingdom. maya Evey Thai Nihitaha Purva Meva -- I have already killed all these people before you decided to start this war. Nimittamatram Bhava Savya Sachin -- so you just become the Nimitta Matra. If somebody gives you credit and says, why dont you become our groups leader and do this petition to such and such? Its not that the guy who is making a petition is the only guy who came up with the idea or we are just giving him a credit.
Look we can all go and talk. You become our leader. Arjuna, Im just giving you this opportunity.
To become the Nimitt Matra because you deserve it. We always choose a person who has the best capabilities or the best qualification to become the representative of our group. We try to elect the best person who could be our president by looking at his qualifications.
So becoming a Nimitta Matra is also something to be very proud of. That somebody has given us a chance considering us to be worthy of it. So when Bhagavan said, you become Nimitta Matra for something, you should take great pride in it and get up and do it., in this case it is Arjuna.
But in our case also, we get this chance all the time. Bhagavan gives us the ability, capability, and opportunity to do something at our level in this world. And Bhagavan saying the same thing, look, I have already done this thing.
It will be done whether you take part in it or not. But you have this opportunity. Why dont you take this chance and become Nimitta Matra? Become the instrument in my hand and take the credit and enjoy the credit.
Bhagavan said to Arjuna, same thing. These people are killed. You just do your part.
You had been trained for these wars, stand up for the right cause. Take your credit and enjoy the fruits. Dronam Chabism Cha Jayadratham cha Karnam Tatha Anyanabi Yodavira maya Hatam Stumhi Jahimam Vyatista.
Nobody gives us this kind of guarantee before we start anything. Rajan, go and do this. You are going to win it. Dont worry about it.
I already took care of it. Once in a while somebody does it for us too. Our father comes and says, Beta, dont worry about it. I already talked to him.
They are going to hire you, right? So Bhagavan said, look, you are worried about a few of them. Whether you admit it or not, you think, how can I fight in front of these great warriors such as Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and Karna? Bhagavan specifically mentions them and says I have already killed them.

Having heard Krishna declare I am Time and I have already killed them, Arjuna responds with trembling, prostration, and choked voice. Sanjaya notes he was overwhelmed with awe, bowing down again and again. Then Arjuna speaks: It is natural that the world revels and rejoices when it sings the praises of Thy glory; the demons fly in fear and the saints offer Thee their salutations. He is processing the vision intellectually while still emotionally shaken.
Notice the different responses to the divine revelation: demons flee in fear, saints offer salutations, and the world rejoices in singing praises. How we respond to truth depends on our nature and readiness. The same reality that terrifies the unprepared becomes a source of devotion for the mature seeker. Arjuna stands at the threshold - shaken but not fleeing, overwhelmed but still present and engaged. This is the response of a genuine seeker: neither running away nor pretending everything is fine.
Reflect today on how you respond to difficult truths. When you encounter the reality of impermanence, do you flee into distraction? When you see the suffering in the world, do you turn away or remain present? The spiritual path is not about achieving a state where nothing disturbs you but about developing the capacity to remain present with whatever arises. Practice today by staying with one uncomfortable truth for just a few minutes longer than you normally would. Notice the impulse to flee and gently remain. This builds the capacity that allows transformation.
